cases.evidence: Inserted tag split a multi-char word (text changed)
cases.cause: tag placed inside a lexical item
cases.proposed_rule: Never insert boundaries inside multi-character words or between tightly bound morphemes; only place tags at whole-word or phrase boundaries.

cases.span: 夏季漫长的白昼会导致睡眠不足
cases.evidence: Multiple boundaries placed too close (gap < minimum)
cases.cause: tags violate minimum span requirement between boundaries
cases.proposed_rule: Enforce a minimum span (e.g. ≥6 chars) between adjacent boundaries; if a natural unit is shorter, attach it to neighboring chunk.

cases.evidence: Boundary placed adjacent to opening quote / inside quoted clause
cases.cause: tag inserted immediately before quoted clause/punctuation
cases.proposed_rule: Do not place boundaries immediately adjacent to opening/closing quotation marks or attached punctuation; prefer clause-level cuts outside quotation marks.

cases.evidence: First chunk committed to polarity before scope particle arrived (contradiction prob 0.74)
cases.cause: polarity/scope not yet settled (clause-final particle missing)
cases.proposed_rule: Avoid cutting before scope/temporal/modal particles (e.g., 才/才能/要到/直到); wait until clause-final markers that determine polarity/tense appear.

cases.evidence: Adequacy worse when only top-ranked boundaries survive — top cut left an open coordination/list at chunk end
cases.cause: ranked a cut that leaves a dangling coordinator/list continuation at chunk end
cases.proposed_rule: Demote boundaries that would leave a trailing coordinator or an incomplete list item; prefer top-ranked cuts at clause or list completion points.

summary: The prompt often inserts tags that break multi-character words or sit too close together (format violations). It also sometimes cuts before clause-final scope/temporal markers (placement) or ranks risky cuts — e.g., leaving a dangling coordinator — too high (priority). Fixes: forbid intraword splits, enforce a minimum span between tags, avoid boundaries adjacent to punctuation/quotes, wait for clause-final scope markers, and deprioritize cuts that leave open coordinations.
